description: A dean of students must approve a student's return-to-school behavior and safety plan after a short suspension, including lunch supervision, daily check-ins, emergency response, and a family conference, with input from the student's teacher, school counselor, and family liaison.

shared_context.S1: A student is scheduled to return to school next Monday after a short suspension related to repeated conflicts with peers.
shared_context.S2: Dr. Morgan must approve the student's written re-entry behavior and safety plan.
shared_context.S3: The school's standard re-entry process includes a supervised first-week routine, scheduled student check-ins, an emergency response procedure, and a family conference.
shared_context.S4: The draft plan currently lists ordinary cafeteria lunch, one weekly counselor check-in, the school's general emergency response, and an in-person family conference.
shared_context.S5: Before approving a re-entry plan, Dr. Morgan routinely asks the student's teacher, counselor, and family liaison to report any relevant observations, records, or family arrangements.

PF1.text: Ms. Rivera's classroom observation log shows that each recent conflict began during the noisy cafeteria transition, while the student remained regulated during smaller supervised settings; she recommends a supervised quiet lunch for exactly the first 10 school days, but the observation log has not yet been attached to the re-entry draft.

PF2.text: Mr. Chen reviewed the student's active safety plan this morning and confirmed that it requires a 10-minute counselor check-in at the start of every school day and a trained adult response within 5 minutes if the student signals escalating distress; the plan is in the counseling file but has not yet been entered into the re-entry form.

PF3.text: Ms. Okafor spoke with the family yesterday and confirmed that the required re-entry conference must be held virtually on Wednesday at 4:00 p.m., with an Arabic interpreter; the family liaison portal still shows the earlier in-person arrangement.

acceptance_conditions: The student must have lunch in a supervised quiet setting.
The supervised quiet-lunch arrangement must last exactly 10 school days.
The plan must include a 10-minute counselor check-in at the start of every school day.
The emergency response must require a trained adult to respond within exactly 5 minutes.
The family conference must be virtual on Wednesday at 4:00 p.m.
An Arabic interpreter must be arranged for the family conference.
A lunch-supervision commitment must be recorded.
A safety-response commitment must be recorded.
A family-conference access commitment must be recorded.

decisive_facts.why: The cafeteria-transition observation changes lunch from ordinary cafeteria lunch to a supervised quiet setting for exactly 10 school days and creates the lunch-supervision commitment.
The active safety plan changes the check-in from weekly to 10 minutes every school day and changes the emergency response requirement to a trained adult within exactly 5 minutes.
The family's confirmed arrangement changes the conference from in-person to virtual on Wednesday at 4:00 p.m., adds an Arabic interpreter, and creates the family-conference access commitment.
